source.title: A Study on the Architectural Form and Characteristics of Tusi Manors in the Yunnan–Tibet Region

humanReview.assessment: Average value. Retain and distill useful architectural evidence, but do not over-promote it.

scope.region: Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, focused on Tibetan-inhabited parts of Deqin County and Shangri-La City
scope.historicalScope: samples reported as built before 1912, with present-day survey and possible later alterations

publishedEvidenceTypes: front, side and rear elevation drawings

materialAndStructuralSystem.coreRelationship: external rammed-earth enclosure with internal timber support appears repeatedly in the surveyed manor group
materialAndStructuralSystem.status: usable only for the Diqing Tusi-manor branch

courtyardTypes: main building enclosed by courtyard walls
main building enclosed by side rooms and courtyard walls
courtyardAndPlan.gateTendency: main gate commonly placed on one side of the courtyard enclosure in the illustrated samples
courtyardAndPlan.status: typology reference, not a universal template

reportedClimateAssociation.flatRoof: dry-hot valley context and crop drying
reportedClimateAssociation.slopedRoof: higher-rainfall alpine context above about 3000 m in the authors' sample interpretation

roof.status: candidate relation requiring independent climatic and measured-roof verification

facadeAndOpenings.frontFacade: more openings and decoration, with door and window lintels emphasized
facadeAndOpenings.sideAndRearFacades: few or small openings, limited decoration
facadeAndOpenings.wallForm: rammed-earth facade commonly represented as wider at the base and narrower at the top
facadeAndOpenings.status: measured comparative ranges for the named samples only

verticalDimensions.status: retain as sample-level evidence; do not average into a province default

verticalTendency: ground floor used for livestock and storage in several samples
middle floor used for living and administration
upper floor commonly contains religious space
functionalOrganization.status: sample-group tendency, not a mandatory assembly rule

defense.status: relevant to Tusi manor defense systems only

qualityLimits: The article is architectural and measured, but publishes a limited comparative sample rather than a complete regional inventory.
Many causal explanations about culture, climate and defense are interpretive and require independent checking.
The authors report precise measurement of structural nodes, yet the paper does not publish a complete construction-node atlas.
Repairs, rebuilding and later alterations are not separated consistently enough for exact historical reconstruction.
The source concerns elite administrative-residential manors and cannot define ordinary vernacular house defaults.
Floor heights, opening ratios and wall forms remain sample evidence until cross-checked against original survey drawings or another independent source.
